messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,

I'm trying to make predictions on Detection probability and my best model has the variable behavior (p0 ~ b). So when I try the get.real appears an error:

pred.df <- data.frame(session = factor(c(1,2)))
pred.det <- get.real(model = best_model, type= "det", newdata = pred.df)

Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'b' not found

Does anyone know how to resolve this error?

Best,
Marina

messages.subject: Effect of trimS on model ranking
messages.subject_clean: Effect of trimS on model ranking
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am running a suite of 14 candidate models in oSCR using rattlesnake data and a very large state space and trap array (40 sessions, each with a SS of around 3000 pixels, with almost 2000 "traps"). Based on other discussions here I recognize that it would be inappropriate to use trimS because I am including spatial covariates of the state space on density itself (which is also why I needed Full Likelihood). My question is, to aid in computation time could I still use trimS on my candidate set without it biasing rankings? I could then re-run just the top ranked model without trimS to get less biased estimates. I have gotten the first 4 models to successfully run, but they took >2 weeks on a high quality computer and I am running into a bottleneck with the more parameterized versions. Thank you so much for your time!

Best,

James

messages.subject: occassion names in EDF not TDF
messages.subject_clean: occassion names in EDF not TDF
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

I have a script from last spring (May 2022) that I'm going back to and I'm encountering this error in data2oscr "some occasion names in EDF not in TDF". This was not an issue the last time I ran the code (IIRC) so I'm just trying to figure out whats going on.

As far as I can tell there aren't any occasion names in the TDF, except for in the usage matrix. My occasions in the tdf are labelled 1:6, while the usage columns are labelled "Usage_X" where X is the occasion (1:6). See screenshots. In some cases a session doesn't start until session 2, or ends at 4, but this historically hasn't caused me any errors.

Is this somehow related to this note in the help?
IMPORTANT NOTE: The column names for the trap deployment columns (cols >= 4) must have the same NAMES as the traps referenced in the encounter data file (EDF).

Sorry, I feel like I should be able to figure this out but I'm not succeeding.

Thanks,
Clayton

messages.subject_clean: Effect of trimS on model ranking
messages.body_plain:
Hi James,

For some reason these group emails are going to my SPAM (sorry to Marina also!).

Having spatial covariates for density should not preclude use of trimS.  The problem is when you have spatial covariates for detection probability (p0).

I think your model selection strategy should be okay, especially if you find correspondence between the trimS and the full version of your top model.  Making pragmatic choices due to computational limitations is always a good excuse, so long as your recognize the risks (which seem low here).

messages.body_plain:
Clayton uncovered a nasty problem when using dplyr as explained here:

https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/group_by.html

Essentially, he had a group by statement to rip the maximum number of occasions from his edf (a good data prep strategy) to calculate session-specific k, but the result was ordering his sessions in a different way than alphabetical.  The help file says you should use the following strategy to combat:

data %>%
  group_by(chr) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(x)) %>%
  arrange(chr, .locale = "en")
